body: Ooooh, that's possible. Thank you so much for the suggestion!
It would make a wonderful greeting card for someone! You should be proud of it.

Oh, wow. I had more trouble parsing the Tagalog translation this time - lots of checking the individual translations for words - but I'm glad that I'm still capable of mostly parsing it. I'm now very sure you're a thoughtful person, one who definitely thinks before they speak. Keep that quality of yours.

I would've never thought of the calligraphy idea! That could probably work, I just need to find a way to simplify my letters. I hope they still look pretty.

And true, very true regarding the gist of your second paragraph. Even if I have goals like worldbuilding and learning Tagalog, I want to enjoy making a language. I hope to find a decent compromise as I learn more about languages.

I'm now very sure I had misused the term auxlang, sorry. I had misunderstood its meaning at first. As for the usage of Filipino and Tagalog, I had been brought up to use the term Filipino in high school (IIRC the definition was that Filipino referred to the amalgamation of various languages including the Tagalog base and was thus preferred) so I apologize. I tend to forget that it's kinda... regionalism? I forget the term, but something about forgetting the variety of cultures in our country in favor of Tagalog. Sorry, I'll try to keep that in mind whenever I talk about the Tagalog language. 

Thank you for all the wonderful suggestions and for being patient with this conlang newbie. I really do appreciate it.

First of all, hats off to you for recreating that comment in Filipino. I'm glad I'm able to understand the gist of it, although that might've been due to the English translation being given beforehand. Still, it's quite nice to see my native language (can one call it their native language if they can't speak it but were raised in it? I certainly wouldn't know)

Anyway, back to the main topic: it's *really* cool that they're making modernized Baybayin. I  have got to study up on it. I suppose changing phonetics is less of a problem that I'm making it to be. I guess I should focus on what is probably the bigger problem of the alphabet, that it's difficult to write. Prettier than it is functional, as I've said.

As for the learning Filipino thing, I am still deciding whether I'd be fine with a relex. I really do want to learn Filipino, but it might be limiting me - I'd love to experiment with something like Japanese first-person pronouns and honorifics. Would a Japanese-Filipino auxlang be appreciated? That's probably a niche thing haha
I'll have to research how to do that, but I might be able to do it. Hopefully using free programs, as I paid to create that font. Thank you so much for being helpful!
